reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch trace the water-versus-ground conflict to a mistranslation of Genesis 1:20, whose Hebrew never actually names an element for the birds.

discrepancy.note: Colenso lists this as one of the plain textual contradictions between Genesis 1 and Genesis 2 as products of two different authors.

quotes.text: In the first, all ' fowls that fl}'' ' are made out of the waters, i.20. In the second, the 'fowls of the air' are made out of the ground, ii.l9.
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Vol. II (1863), Signs of Different Authors in the Pentateuch, on Genesis 1:20 and Genesis 2:19.

sides.snippet: the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of sky
sides.verseText: God said, \"Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of sky.\"

sides.snippet: Out of the ground Yahweh God formed every animal of the field, and every bird of the sky
sides.verseText: Out of the ground Yahweh God formed every animal of the field, and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the man to see what he would call them. Whatever the man called every living creature, that was its name.
